summary: Python FastAPI MES framework (540 commits, last commit 2026-11-05) with 21 plugin directories, Vite/React 19 clients, a time-interval OEE calculation, and no runtime AI, no tenancy, no CI and no Temporal/Rust edge, so it diverges from the GreyHook benchmark on most multi-tenant, AI and security dimensions.

d1_oee.formula: OEE = Availability x Performance x Quality, computed in OEEService.calculate_oee (server/src/mes/core/performance/service.py, ~lines 342-500). Availability = run_time / (run_time + downtime_planned + downtime_unplanned), where run_time = uptime_value_add + uptime_non_value. Performance = min((ideal_cycle_time x total_count) / run_time, 1.0). Quality = good / (good + reject + rework). Matches the benchmark formula.
d1_oee.storage: Not stored as OEE rows; computed on read from equipment_state_logs (interval overlap clipped to the query period) and production counters (good, reject, rework, ideal_cycle_time_sec). Models in server/src/mes/core/performance/models.py. Ideal cycle time resolves from EquipmentMaterial.design_speed converted via the UoM right_uom multiplier, else ProductionCounter average, else 0. Exposed at GET /api/v1/performance/oee and published as an oee_calculated event.
gaps: Only performance is clamped (min upper bound to 1.0); availability and quality are not clamped to [0,1] and performance has no lower-bound guard
When no state logs exist availability returns 0.0, but equipment with no state model is treated as 100% available (engine.py DEFAULT_STATE), an inconsistent default
No ISO 22400 reference found in the files read; the docstring cites the Six Big Losses model
Ideal cycle time falls back to 3600 / design_speed when the UoM lookup fails, silently assuming an hourly rate
Performance is capped silently at 1.0 instead of flagging an incorrect ideal cycle time

state_enum: Plugin-defined states; default 'running' when no state model is assigned (engine.py DEFAULT_STATE)

PackML ISA-TR88 (17): Stopped, Resetting, Idle, Starting, Execute, Completing, Complete, Holding, Held, Unholding, Suspending, Suspended, Unsuspending, Stopping, Aborting, Aborted, Clearing, plus Stopped
SEMI E10 (6): Productive, Standby, Engineering, Scheduled Downtime, Unscheduled Downtime, Non-Scheduled
Canonical dispatch_category: available, busy, unavailable_planned, unavailable_unplanned
Canonical oee_bucket: uptime_value_add, uptime_non_value, downtime_planned, downtime_unplanned, excluded
d2_downtime.model: Event/interval model. EquipmentStateLog rows carry started_at and ended_at (null = open). Each row is mapped to dispatch_category and oee_bucket at write time. Transitions are validated against the registered state model's transition table (engine.py). OEE is time-weighted over the interval overlap, not sampled periodically.
schema_fields: Reason: code (4 chars), name, oee_bucket, parent_id (hierarchical tree)
gaps: No running / idle / fault / offline enum; states are plugin-defined and the canonical categories differ from the benchmark
No offline state; a disconnected machine is not modelled as a state
Equipment without a state model defaults to running (100% available), so unmonitored equipment looks healthy
Downtime categorisation depends on manual Reason assignment and plugin mappings; no automatic fault taxonomy found

protocols: Kafka via native SDK sidecar (plugins/system/kafka_java_bridge; gRPC on 127.0.0.1:50051)
d3_device.edge_arch: No Rust edge gateway in the repo (no .rs or Cargo.toml files). Drivers are in-process Python plugins under server/plugins/system/, each with manifest.yaml and plugin.py, subclassing MESPlugin (server/src/mes/framework/plugin/base.py) with 12 ExtensionPointType values. SDK-only systems run as a child-process sidecar with a gRPC contract (HealthCheck, Publish, Subscribe). Plugins are loaded in-process via importlib spec_from_file_location and exec_module (framework/plugin/manager.py ~lines 219-241).
d3_device.write_guard: None found. write_tag() exists on the OPC-UA, MQTT, Modbus and AVEVA adapters; OPC-UA tags are classified readwrite or write from AccessLevel. No read-only or write-enable flag was found in the files read, and no caller of write_tag was seen, so the write path could not be fully traced. MQTT writes publish with retain=True.
gaps: OPC-UA defaults to security mode none and anonymous auth (opcua/config.py lines 39-41)
MQTT TLS is off by default (mqtt/config.py EQUIP_MQTT_USE_TLS=False); QoS defaults to 1 and is validated to 0-2
No write-back guard or read-only mode per plugin or per tag
The '13-protocol' claim is not supported: 9 distinct transport/integration plugins, plus 2 state-model plugins (PackML, SEMI E10), simulators, mocks and an example plugin across 21 plugin directories
Kafka is reached through a Java sidecar, not a native Python Kafka client; consumer idempotency not evidenced in the files read

d4_data_model.hierarchy: Site > Area > Line > WorkCell > Equipment, with EquipmentMaterial (physical_model routes under /api/v1: /sites, /areas, /lines, /work-cells, /equipment). Products and routes in core/product_def and core/routing; lots and units in core/wip/models.py.
d4_data_model.shift_model: WorkSchedule with WorkShift, ShiftBreak, WorkRotation with RotationSegment, WorkTeam with TeamMember and TeamMemberException, and NonWorkingPeriod (server/src/mes/core/work_schedule/models.py). Production counters are shift-level per the ProductionCounter docstring.
order_states: Operations order: created, released, in_progress, completed, closed (core/operations/models.py)
Work schedule: draft, released, active, closed
WIP unit and lot: queued, in_process, completed, finished, scrapped, on_hold (core/wip/models.py)
d4_data_model.telemetry_schema: ProductionCounter (shift-level good, reject and rework counts, ideal_cycle_time_sec, per equipment and product) and EquipmentStateLog (interval state records). No TimescaleDB or hypertable: the 2026-05-12 baseline migration and the 2026-07-08 performance migration contain no references. Storage is plain PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy 2 async and Alembic.
d4_data_model.tenancy: Single-tenant. No organization_id or tenant column in the baseline migration (0 matches across 63 create_table calls) or in the files read. Cross-org isolation is not implemented.

d5_api.versioning: /api/v1 prefix on every router seen: /api/v1/performance, /api/v1 for physical model, /api/v1/events/ws for WebSocket. No v2 found.
d5_api.realtime: WebSocket at /api/v1/events/ws (server/src/mes/framework/events/gateway.py). Client sends {action: subscribe, topics: [...]} with fnmatch-style topic patterns, or {action: ping}. There is no dedicated machine-status channel; equipment_state_changed events are carried on the general bus.
d5_api.envelope: MESEvent JSON: {event_id, event_type (dot-notation topic), timestamp (UTC), source, payload {}, correlation_id}, serialized with model_dump(mode=json) (framework/events/schema.py and gateway.py broadcast).
d5_api.auth: Local login issues HS256 JWT access tokens (15 min) and refresh tokens (7 days); passwords hashed with PBKDF2-SHA256 (framework/auth/service.py). RBAC via require_permission('perm') on routes, e.g. performance.read and wip.unit.move (framework/auth/dependencies.py). OIDC mode is configured in config.py and .env.example but was not verified. config.py defaults AUTH_MODE to 'none', which disables auth entirely, and the WebSocket endpoint performs no token check.

gaps: No runtime AI integration: no LLM module, no Anthropic/OpenAI SDK and no MCP tools in the repo tree or server/pyproject.toml
No tenant isolation exists to enforce on AI queries
README describes AI only as a development-time workflow (AI-assisted coding and testing)

d7_quality.tests: 53 unit test files under server/tests/unit (pytest, pytest-asyncio and pytest-cov declared in server/pyproject.toml), plus 23 SQA module files under SQA/ (Playwright and pytest end-to-end flows for design-time and runtime). Coverage percentage not measured.
d7_quality.migrations: Alembic: 9 revision files under server/alembic/versions/, starting from a 2026-05-12 baseline (63 create_table calls) followed by 8 incremental revisions (performance indexes and views, segment parameter values, tracking override, dashboard alert rules). Downgrade functions not verified.
security_flags: config.py line 29 defaults AUTH_MODE to 'none'; every request becomes a synthetic admin 'dev-admin' and permission checks are skipped (framework/auth/dependencies.py)
A default admin user with password 'admin' is seeded at startup (main.py calls seed_admin_user unconditionally; framework/auth/service.py ~lines 243-247)
SECRET_KEY defaults to the placeholder 'CHANGE_ME_IN_PRODUCTION' (config.py line 30)
Default database credentials postgres:postgres in config.py line 23 and .env.example
WebSocket /api/v1/events/ws accepts connections without a token and streams all events (events/gateway.py)
OPC-UA defaults to security none and anonymous auth (opcua/config.py lines 39-41)
MQTT TLS off by default (mqtt/config.py line 36)

Simulate endpoints (simulate-opcua-state, simulate-mqtt-counts, simulate-historian-state and others) sit on the production performance router (performance/routes.py lines 251-493) with no feature-flag gate seen
Plugin code executes in-process via exec_module from plugins/system with no signing or sandbox (framework/plugin/manager.py)
Doc/code mismatch: a docstring in auth/service.py says bcrypt while the code uses PBKDF2-SHA256 (ARCHITECTURE.md also says PBKDF2)
d7_quality.last_active: 2026-11-05 (commit: 'Enhanced the runtime dashboard to include production trends, loss drill-down and configurable alerts', v1.9.1)

adopt: Per-plugin manifest.yaml plus MESPlugin ABC with a typed ExtensionPointType enum (framework/plugin/base.py), matching the registry-over-branches rule

PackML ISA-TR88 and SEMI E10 mapped to canonical dispatch_category and oee_bucket at write time (performance/engine.py, packml_availability, semi_e10_availability) as a mapping layer for running/idle/fault/offline
Interval-based OEE with clipping to the query period (performance/service.py ~lines 404-408)
Ideal cycle time from nameplate design_speed with UoM conversion (resolve_ideal_cycle_time)
Native SDK sidecar over gRPC with HealthCheck/Publish/Subscribe for SDK-only systems (NativeSdkBridgePlugin, kafka_java_bridge)
Topic-filtered WebSocket with a canonical MESEvent envelope including correlation_id (events/schema.py, gateway.py)
Reason code hierarchy carrying an oee_bucket per reason (performance/models.py)
avoid: AUTH_MODE default 'none' combined with an admin/admin seed; use fail-closed auth and forced first-run credentials
Unauthenticated WebSocket stream of all events
OPC-UA security none and anonymous by default; MQTT TLS off by default
Availability 0.0 without logs versus 100% without a state model (inconsistent defaults)
In-process exec_module of plugin code without signing or sandboxing
No CI workflows in the repo
differentiate: Multi-tenant organization_id on every row with cross-org 404; this repo has none
Rust edge gateway with outbound-only connectivity and a telemetry processor; this repo has no Rust, and its Kafka path is a Java sidecar

Kafka as the native streaming backbone with idempotent consumers; the repo's bus defaults to in-memory (MES_EVENT_BUS_TYPE=memory), with redis, kafka and nats only designed for (ARCHITECTURE.md line 283)
Temporal workflows for retries and partial failures; the repo has none
Read-only, rate-limited AI (claude-sonnet-4-6) through approved parameterized tool functions; the repo has no runtime AI
Stack: Vite + React 19 rather than Next.js 15; no Temporal, no TimescaleDB; PostgreSQL plus SQL Server and Oracle per README (not verified in code)
Machine connectivity read-only by default with an enforced write-back guard; this repo's write_tag has no guard
